title: Bootstrapped founder report: revenue drop, burnout, and shipping a portfolio of AI products
summary: John Rush shares a raw update across his SaaS portfolio: a 20% revenue drop, a comaker burnout, and many shipped features. Useful lessons: cut low-value pricing tiers, build experimentation into products, bundle agents in a store, and recruit beta testers publicly.

principles.text: Remove the cheapest plan to filter out difficult users who drain support.
principles.quote: Removed the $19 plan to cut out “difficult users” who drain my support agents

principles.text: Build automated experimentation into the product: the agent generates campaigns, copy and media to find what converts.
principles.quote: shipped A/B testing engine inside **[tinyadz.com](https://tinyadz.com/)** (the agent keeps coming up with different campaigns/copy/media to find what converts best

principles.text: Recruit beta testers by asking for a public comment, then DM them.
principles.quote: beta launched socialbot for my product accounts on social media, I need 10 beta testers now, reply with a comment and I’ll DM u

principles.text: Make your product ecosystem easy to adopt: one-click install of all your agents from an in-platform store.
principles.quote: launched an “Agent Store” inside unicorn platform. It’s so cool. You can install all my agents with just one click inside there.

principles.text: Share the bad alongside the good in founder reports; the rawness engages readers.
Move the business to lower-tax jurisdictions to keep more of what you earn.
principles.quote: started moving my biz from US to Dubai (to save on taxes)
